## Solution

We evaluate
$$L = \lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{\int_0^2\left(\frac{x^n+1}{x^n+2}\right)^n dx}.$$

Set $I_n = \int_0^2\left(\frac{x^n+1}{x^n+2}\right)^n dx$ and $f_n(x)=\frac{x^n+1}{x^n+2}$.

**Upper bound.** Since $x^n+1 \leq x^n+2$, we have $0 < f_n(x) \leq 1$ for all $x\in[0,2]$. Hence $f_n(x)^n \leq 1$ and
$$I_n \leq \int_0^2 1\,dx = 2 \implies I_n^{1/n} \leq 2^{1/n}\to 1.$$

**Lower bound.** Fix any $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$. For $x\in[1+\varepsilon,\,2]$ we have $x^n\ge(1+\varepsilon)^n$, so
$$f_n(x)=1-\frac{1}{x^n+2}\ge 1-\frac{1}{(1+\varepsilon)^n+2}=:1-a_n,$$
where $a_n=\frac{1}{(1+\varepsilon)^n+2}\to 0$ exponentially. Therefore
$$I_n\ge\int_{1+\varepsilon}^{2}(1-a_n)^n\,dx = (1-\varepsilon)(1-a_n)^n.$$

Now $n\,a_n = \frac{n}{(1+\varepsilon)^n+2}\to 0$ (exponential beats linear), so
$$n\ln(1-a_n)\sim -n\,a_n\to 0 \implies (1-a_n)^n\to e^0=1.$$

Taking $n$-th roots:
$$I_n^{1/n}\ge (1-\varepsilon)^{1/n}\cdot(1-a_n)\to 1\cdot 1=1.$$

**Conclusion.** For every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$1\le\liminf_{n\to\infty} I_n^{1/n}\le\limsup_{n\to\infty} I_n^{1/n}\le 1,$$
so by the squeeze theorem
$$\boxed{L=1}.$$
